summary: Julius Eggeling was an Indology scholar who studied at Breslau and Berlin (1862–1866) under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and as a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen (1857–1861) under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Heinrich Meier, later serving as director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire and professor at the University of Strasbourg.

Julius Grill was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Tübingen and Jena, working under Adalbert Kuhn and Rudolf von Roth, and later served as Professor of Old Testament Exegesis at the University of Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Jolly was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Munich, Berlin, Leipzig, and Würzburg under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1882–1883) and as a professor at Würzburg (1877–1920).

Julius Lipner is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, Jadavpur University, Birmingham, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. He taught at Birmingham and was Professor of Hinduism and Comparative Religion at Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological studies. After studying at the University of Tübingen, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, he held professorships at Tübingen (1826–1834) and the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Breslau, Berlin, and Göttingen between 1819 and 1823. He later held academic posts at Göttingen (~1831–1835), Marburg (~1835–1839), and Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied under Rudolf Much at the University of Vienna (~1905–1911). His career included academic posts at the universities of Vienna, Berlin, Bern, Zurich, and Munich.
Julius Schubring studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1857–1858), the University of Göttingen (~1858–1860), and the University of Bonn (~1860–1862).

Jun Fujii is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a doctorate in literature at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2007). He later served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University (~2009–2013).

Jun Takashima specializes in Indology, religious studies, and computational studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and later held posts at Aichi Prefectural University and as a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2020).

Jun Yang is a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Yang held posts as a Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University.

Jun'ichi Oda is a scholar of linguistics and computational studies who studied at the University of Tsukuba. He later held posts at Shobi University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1993–2021).

Jundo Nagashima is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Alexis Sanderson, and Paul Williams, earning a PhD at the University of Bristol, and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2006–2017).

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston.

Junglan Bang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under Harunaga Isaacson at the University of Hamburg (PhD 2012), also studying under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn. Bang later served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ha completed a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and earned a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe (attested 2016).

Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Berlin, and Leipzig under Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served as professor and president at the University of Tokyo and headed several educational institutions.

Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Toyo University (~1891–1894), founded Sogenkutsu in 1892, and served as a professor at both Toyo University and Komazawa University, as well as at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Hokkaido University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
